To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the price-cap regulation approach to public utility pricing is optimal, and (2) this approach is robust to the presence of uncertainty, nonhomogeneous technology, and the need to optimize reliability of supply.

(1) the optimal capacity is the capacity which maximizes expected net benefits (ENB), (2) the optimal price is the price that maximizes expected net revenue (ENR), (3) the optimal reliability is the reliability that maximizes the ENB, and (4) the optimal reliability depends on the price, and vice versa.

the optimal price and capacity are functions of the probability distribution of demand and the probability distribution of the cost of supply interruptions, and that the optimal reliability of supply is a function of the price of capacity and the price of supply interruptions, as well as the probability distribution of supply interruptions.

the optimal design of electric power systems.
the problem of designing optimal public utility pricing policies and capacity investment plans under uncertainty and/or non-homogeneous technology.
the development of optimal rules for the pricing and capacity investment decisions of a monopolistic public utility in the presence of demand and supply uncertainty.

the optimal public utility investment policy is to invest in the capacity that minimizes the sum of the discounted present values of all future costs, where future costs are the sum of the costs of operating the system and the costs associated with the probability of supply interruption.

the literature has not provided a consistent set of recommendations for optimal pricing, capacity, and investment.
